Complainant versus A-1) Sh. Uttam Singh S/o. Sh. Bhagwan Singh [Since Expired] A-2) Sh. Harmeet Singh S/o. Sh. Uttam Singh R/o. B-33, Gujranwala Town, Delhi- 09 A-3) M/s. texts.facts: Accused Persons Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the Pfa Act and Rules . The accused no.1 (since expired) and accused no.2 are stated to be the partners of accused no.3 partnership firm that that supplied the food article, that is, 'Tea' to the vendor Sh. Satya Dev Gupta from whom it was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 16.05.2006, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) Gian Chand and Field Assistant (FA) J. P. Bhardwaj under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. Yogesh Pratap reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. Shyam Cigarrette Store at 18A, Kamla Nagar, Delhi - 07, where one Sh. Satya Dev Gupta was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Tea from the vendor as lying in sealed pouches of 250 gram each bearing identical label declaration and In Re vs A-1) Sh. Uttam Singh on 20 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75769972/ 1 batch number, to which he agreed. A sample of three such packets of Tea was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including Notice as per Form-VI, panchnama. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 24.05.2006, the PA found the sample to be 'misbranded' because the language of best before declaration was not as per Rule 32(i) of PFA Rules. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI. Investigation revealed that the vendor Satya Dev Gupta was the proprietor of M/s. Shyam Cigarette Store, who had purchased the food article from M/s. Uttam Singh & Sons (accused no.3 partnership firm herein). The said partnership firm was having two partners i.e. Sh. Harmeet Singh (accused no.2 herein) and Sh. Uttam Singh (accused no.1 herein, since expired). It was further found that the food article had been manufactured / packed by a company M/s. Uttam Singh Tea Company Pvt. Ltd., of which Sh. Harmeet Singh (accused no.2 herein) and Sh. Ramneet Singh were the Directors. 3. At the time of lifting of sample, there was a policy of the complainant department bearing no.F6(228)/85/ENF./PFA dated 23.09.1985 according to which no prosecution was to be launched against first violators of Rule 32 and instead, only a warning in writing was to be issued. Though the said policy was subsequently withdrawn vide office order no.5/07 dated 14.09.2007, yet the said policy was in operation on the day of lifting the sample. 4. The investigation revealed that the vendor Satya Dev Gupta, the manufacturing company M/s. Uttam Singh Tea Company Pvt. Ltd., and its Directors Sh. Harmeet Singh (accused no. 2 herein) and Sh. Ramneet Singh were the first violators of Rule 32 and in compliance with the above policy, a warning was issued to them and no prosecution was launched against them. However, it was found that Sh. Harmeet Singh (accused no.2 herein in the capacity of partner) along with the partnership firm accused no.3 had already been issued a warning vide letter no. F- 6(901)/94/PFA/7420-21 dated 29.09.2004 by the LHA. As the said firm and its partners were not the first violators of Rule 32, they were not entitled to the benefit of policy. Thus, after completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 01.09.2006 against the supplier firm accused no.3 and its two partners accused no.1 and 2, alleging violation of section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act read with Rule 32(i) of PFA Rules, as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 5. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned vide order dated 01.09.2006. 6. Accused no.1 expired during the pendency of the case on 13.05.2009 and proceedings against him stood abated, as per order dated 05.04.2010. Based on the report of PA, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed against the accused no.2 and 3 vide order dated 13.08.2010 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act, being violation of section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. In Re vs A-1) Sh. Uttam Singh on 20 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75769972/ 2 7. At the trial, prosecution examined four witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 FI Sh. Gian Chan, PW-2 Sh. Yogesh Pratap (SDM/LHA) and PW-3 FA J. P. Bhardwaj were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 16.05.2006 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of three sealed packets of Tea (Uttam brand) of 250 gram each, dividing it in three parts after considering one packet as one counterpart, fastening, sealing, marking the sample counterparts, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, Notice under section 14A Ex. PW-1/D, Raid Report Ex. PW-1/D-1, PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/E and LHA receipt Ex. PW- 1/F. PA report Ex. PW-1/G was received and investigation was conducted by PW-1 who sent letter Ex. PW-1/H to the vendor and received its reply Ex. PW-1/H-1 along with some documents. He sent letter Ex. PW-1/I to VAT Officer and received its reply. He sent letter Ex. PW-1/J to accused no.3 and received its reply Ex. PW-1/J along with copy of the bill and other documents. Letter Ex. PW-1/K was written to the STO and the particulars of the partners of accused no.3 were ascertained. Similarly, letter Ex. PW-1/K-1 was sent to STO to ascertain the constitution of the manufacturing company and its reply was received. Letter Ex. PW-1/K-2 was also sent to the said company which was replied vide letter Ex. PW- 1/K-3 thereby confirming the sale of food article to accused no.3 herein vide bill no. 32 dated 06.05.2006. After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW-1/L was taken from the Director PFA and thereafter, complaint Ex. PW-1/M was filed in the court. A copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex. PW-1/N was sent to the accused persons vide postal receipt Ex. PW-1/O. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by the Ld. Defence Counsel for accused no.2 and 3 wherein they denied that no previous warning was served upon the accused persons. 8. The complainant also examined PW-4 Sh. R. P. Singh who produced the record of issuance of warning letter to accused no.2 and 3 on 29.09.1994 by the then LHA Sh. R. K. Ahuja. Copy of the same Ex. PW- 4/A and dak register Ex. PW-4/B were proved. 9. Statement of the accused no.2 (also representing accused no.3 firm as its AR) under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 22.09.2014 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. He expressed ignorance about the sample proceedings, though questioned the PA report claiming that there was no misbranding. He stated that no warning letter was ever issued to him and also alleged that the vendor might be selling spurious / duplicate products. He chose to lead evidence in defence. 10. The accused persons summoned the record of telephone bill from MTNL through DW-1 Sh. Rajinder Singh. He proved the record Ex. DW- 1/A and Ex. DW-1/B, where the address of accused no. 1 was mentioned as "Shop No. 6313, 9A, Kamla Nagar, Delhi- 07". Similarly, record of electricity bill Ex. DW-2/A to Ex. DW-2/D was proved by DW-2 Sh. S. S. Negi from TPDDL. Record of MCD was also proved as Ex. DW-3/A through DW-3 Sh. Shivender Singh.
texts.arguments: 11. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt as all the witnesses have supported its case and no material contradiction can be seen in their testimonies. It In Re vs A-1) Sh. Uttam Singh on 20 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75769972/ 3 is submitted that the accused persons have failed to rebut the findings of the PA report which shows that the sample was misbranded being in violation of the packaging and labelling rules. It is also contended that the record clearly establishes that the accused persons were not the first violators and are thus liable to be prosecuted. 12. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has argued that no case is made out against the accused persons. Ld. Counsel has submitted that date of packing was given on the label and therefore, the best before declaration could be ascertained easily without any problem. It is thus contended that there is no violation of Rule 32(i) because the words "best before 12 months" read together with the declaration "month and year packed- 3/06" would be sufficient to convey the meaning, even if the exact language of Rule 32(i) "best before 12 months from packaging / manufacture" was not used. It is then submitted that the accused persons had never received and previous warning as per the policy of the complainant and therefore, they were also entitled to be given warning in writing instead of launching the prosecution. 13. In the judgement titled as Ram Babu Rastogi v. State [2012 (1) FAC 56 (Delhi High Court)], the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi held that the objective of declaration on the label was that the purchaser should know at the time of purchase, as to whether the article, which is purchased was capable of being as used and till what time. The Hon'ble High Court was dealing with a position In Re vs A-1) Sh. Uttam Singh on 20 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75769972/ 4 where the actual label of the sample was "Best Before within 6 months from the date of packing" as against the required language "Best Before 6 months from the date of packing". It was held that the language so used conveyed much more than what was required to be conveyed to the purchaser about the genuineness of the product. It was held that mere use of the word "within" as a surplusage would not bring the petitioners under the penal provisions of the Act, as by any means, the purchasers could not be said to have been deceived or misled as regards the character, quantity, quality, or date of manufacture and the limit of use of the product. Therefore, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi [LEAKAGE_MASK] the proceedings in that matter. 20. Same was the position in the judgements titled as Nehrudasan v. Food Inspector, Madurai [2010(1) FAC 49 (Madras High Court)], A. Rajasingh v. Food Inspector [2008(1) FAC 172 (Madras High Court)], T. Prabhu v. The Madras State [2007(1) FAC 314 (Madras High Court)] and Hindustan Lever Limited v. Food Inspector [2007(1) FAC 299 (Madras High Court)]. 28. Section 19(2) of PFA Act provides that a vendor shall not be deemed to have committed an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food if he proves that he had purchased the food article from any manufacturer, distributor or dealer with a written warranty in the prescribed form, and that the said article of food while in his possession was properly stored and that he sold it in the same state as he purchased it. 29. But no prosecution has been launched against the said company or its directors, due to existence of policy of the complainant, which has been recognized by the High Court of Delhi in S. S. Gokul Krishnan v. State [2009(1) FAC 132] and other precedents.
